title: TS SDK: AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams conformance suite and narrative examples
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: deliver a compact, executable conformance suite and a set of narrative examples that validate and document the TypeScript SDK's interop surface between AsyncIterator-style consumers (AsyncIterable/AsyncIterator) and Web Streams (ReadableStream/TransformStream).

Scope:
- Define a small, well-documented adapter contract: convertToReadableStream(asyncIterable, options) and convertToAsyncIterable(readableStream, options).
- Specify exact semantics for: backpressure (pull vs push), cancellation propagation (abort signals / errors), error propagation, single-consumer enforcement, and early termination cleanup.
- Implement deterministic integration tests that run across Node (>=18), Deno, and Chrome via Playwright to catch runtime differences (backpressure semantics, microtask scheduling).
- Deliver narrative examples aimed at SDK users: streaming generation (server -> client), client-side transformers (request body as ReadableStream), and graceful reconnect patterns for resumable outputs.

Motivation:
Teams keep hitting subtle differences when bridging AsyncIterable and Web Streams: chunk boundaries, when pull() is invoked, how stream.cancel() maps to iterator.return(), and whether errors thrown in a transformer end up as stream errors or swallowed promises. This task reduces customer friction by making interop deterministic and well-tested, plus providing copy-paste examples for common patterns.

Non-goals:
- Implementing resumable token-level checkpoints (separate epic).
- Adding new runtime shims for older Node versions (<18).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter API signatures documented and stable: convertToReadableStream(asyncIterable, opts) and convertToAsyncIterable(readable, opts)
Conformance suite with >= 20 deterministic tests covering: chunking, backpressure, cancellation, error propagation, multi-consumer rejections, and transform passthrough
CI runs the suite in Node 18/20, Deno stable, and Chrome (headless) and fails on any spec delta
Examples published in SDK docs (2 short guides + 3 runnable examples in examples/streaming/)
Performance regression: adapter adds <5% overhead in token-throughput microbench compared to baseline direct runtime plumbing
Design doc reviewed and approved by API/Runtime team (sign-off comment in PR)
comments: 2025-03-10 - Ava Chen: Kickoff. Spike found inconsistent cancellation behavior between Node's ReadableStream and browser ReadableStream when iterator.return() is called. See notes in linked doc.

2025-03-11 - Diego Morales: Prototype implemented for convertToReadableStream; uses ReadableStream's pull() to await next() on the AsyncIterator and maps iterator.return() to controller.close()/controller.error(). Found that Node schedules pull earlier — added microtask yield to normalize timing.
2025-03-11 - Diego Morales: Ran simple throughput bench. Overhead ~2.2% on synthetic token stream with highWaterMark=1. Good initial signal.

2025-03-12 - Design review: Decided to expose two normalization options in the API: strictBackpressure (pull-when-demand) and relaxedThroughput (prefetch up to highWaterMark). Both are boolean flags; default is strictBackpressure for predictable latency-sensitive usage.
2025-03-12 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 - contains adapter impl, unit tests, and basic docs. Needs cross-runtime CI config.
